title: A Decision-Support Framework for the Management of Water Distribution Networks by Integrating SCADA Data, Measurement Uncertainty and EPANET Hydraulic Modelling
content: Water utilities increasingly operate SCADA systems reporting network state in real time, yet data is not the same as enough: a measurement adequate for one decision may be useless for another. As a proof of concept, we develop a decision-support framework linking measurement, uncertainty evaluation, hydraulic modelling and the decision in one chain, demonstrated on two tasks: loss detection and judging whether a network can absorb a new demand. On a laboratory rig, flow through orifices of 2.07, 3.12 and 4.07 mm measured diameter was measured as the difference of two in-line readings. A conservative worst-case combination of the meter accuracy limits yields a loss-uncertainty band falling from ±48–55% at 2.07 mm to ±13–15% at 4.07 mm, so detectability depends less on the instrument than on the ratio between loss and transit flow. The discharge coefficient, recomputed with the measured diameters and upstream head, settles at 0.64–0.68 and serves only as a physical bridge to EPANET, not a precise metrological figure. In a demonstrative DMA, a ±20% change in the loss shifts the admissible new-demand limit by only ±0.14 L/s, the decision changing only within a thin band around the threshold. The central proposal is an adequacy test: precision is sufficient whenever propagating its uncertainty leaves the decision classification unchanged, letting the framework judge a decision's robustness and whether extra instrumentation would help.
